item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I actually liked the way that this story was written. It was simple and reminded me of Goosebumps, which, for me, made me feel nostalgic in a weird way.

I know 096 is supposed to be a mindless monster, but this story actually came across as strangely tragic. Maybe it's the fact that such an iconic SCP was brought low in such an unceremonious manner, or maybe it's the way that 096's death was described, showing the suffering and agony of a creature being punished simply for following its nature and instincts.

In either case, if this was a tale to show why the Foundation doesn't "destroy, destroy, destroy," its anomalies (especially the sentient ones), it does a pretty good job in doing so.

+1

item.title: Re: Finally
item.content:encoded:
I agree that foundation needs to actually kill an scp to show that they are controlling things instead of barely containing.

Firstly, the Foundation is not the Global Occult Coalition. The Foundation is very cautious of destroying anomalies because sometimes the consequences can be severe.

Secondly, the Foundation have killed several SCPs (could be found under Neutralized), even wiping out populations of some to make them only exist in Foundation containment. Below is some examples:

  • SCP-966 — (Sleep Killer)
  • SCP-745 — (The Headlights)
  • SCP-939 — (With Many Voices)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Warning potentially controversial idea coming I would be glad if became canon and SCP-096 was terminated for multiple reasons, which will be listed below;

  • It's about time the Foundation was actually successful in killing a seemingly SCP like 096, it demonstrates a decent level of competence among them and how much they've progressed since they initially contained it.
  • Killing off a Series 1 vet may encourage others to pay more attention to the newer and lesser-known SCPs, broadening the community's horizons.
  • SCP-173 assisting in the termination demonstrates its usefulness and explains why they haven't attempted to terminate it yet.
  • SCP-096 is fairly overrated in my opinion, sure it's terrifying beyond belief, but it doesn't have much a backstory as far as I know and doesn't do much in the lore of the SCP universe.

they will at least link here instead of some random unpublished low quality knockoff of the 682 termination log sandboxed draft.

*Finds said sandbox draft, checks its history just to be sure* Huh.

So yeah, it's the weirdest damn thing. I made this three and a half years ago when I was a relative newbie, before I had successfully posted anything yet alone was a regular contributor. I can't say it's not a knockoff of 682's log, and I can't say it's good either, which is why I abandoned it shortly after making it.

And yet, somehow a low quality, abandoned sandbox draft eventually seeped out into the community's collective consciousness enough for SCP Illustrated to make a video of it, and for it to at least have partially inspired this tale, including the oddly specific detail of 173 snapping 096's neck for five hours.

Weirdest damn thing.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Upvoted mainly for presentation, rather than content, and I suppose also because when people on reddit insist on the "canonicity" of this event, they will at least link here instead of some random unpublished low quality knockoff of the 682 termination log sandboxed draft.

I think there's some good parts here, Daniels is at least marginally developed as a character, and the denouement had a good feel of sloppy verisimilitude about it.

Where this fails, is that I don't think that I really care if 096 was ever terminated or not and this doesn't really make much effort to sell it to me. I don't especially find the object itself very compelling, I don't have any interest in using it for anything1, and I am content to imagine that any given Foundation either doesn't have one, neutralized it years ago without fanfare, or has it Euclid contained without further incident.

Which just means that I wasn't the target audience for this.

This does present a bit of a continuity conundrum, in that it's hard to imagine why the Foundation cares about destroying this one particular thing (which is pretty solidly contained in total darkness now) when they seem committed to unstable Keter containment of many worse ones, but that's probably just a hobgoblin of small minds.

Footnotes
1. Except, goddammit, I of course just thought of an idea, for an origin story of all things. Brains, whatcha gonna do, amirite?
